# CI and release

The jobs of the workflow and the release of the binaries. Moved from the root `CLAUDE.md` with its wording unchanged; the root file says where each area lives.

CI jobs (wave 023, run 0176, W-14): `.github/workflows/ci-build.yaml` runs the checks of a change as a job `Changes`, four jobs that need it and run in parallel, and a last one, so that the time of CI is the slowest part and not the sum. `Changes` (checkout, `fetch-depth` `'0'` on a pull request and `'1'` otherwise, as the strings of the expression because the number `0` is falsy; step "Work out which parts apply") runs `node scripts/changes.mjs --event "$EVENT" --base "$BASE_SHA" --head "$HEAD_SHA"` and outputs `java`, `page`, `kernel` and `e2e`, each `true` or `false`, with a summary of the decision (a table of the four jobs with the rule that raised each, and the changed paths that fell to the default rule). Only a pull request is filtered: a push to `main`, a tag and any diff that is empty or fails give four `true`, and a `workflow_dispatch` runs none of them. Each of the four jobs has `needs: Changes` and runs when its output is `true`. The map is `RULES` in `scripts/changes.mjs`, the first rule that matches a path wins, a path with no rule runs all four (the last rule), and `src/test/javascript/changes-map.test.js` audits it (every tracked path has a rule, the rules agree with what each job reads) and runs the gate of `Build`; a file added to the repository that a job reads needs a rule, or it runs everything. A pull request that edits `.github/**` or `scripts/changes.mjs` runs all four (rule R-06), so one that changes the filter itself runs everything. `Java`: `./mvnw verify` (step "Build artifacts") and "Keep the Java coverage report" (and, on a tag, the artifact `manual` = `target/generated-docs`, which the website takes). `Page` (Node 22, `fetch-depth: 0` because tests run `git show archicode-0.17.0:...`): `npm ci`, "Check the format", "Lint the JavaScript", "Cover the editor script", "Keep the editor coverage report", "Check the time budget of the kernel". `Kernel` (rustup only): "Test the viewpoint kernel", fmt, clippy, "Install cargo-llvm-cov", "Cover the viewpoint kernel", "Check the committed WebAssembly is the one the Rust builds". `E2E`: its own jar, the Playwright browsers (three: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and the cache key names them), "Run the end-to-end tests" (see the end-to-end paragraph below). `Build` needs `Changes` and the four, its first step ("Check that every part ran or was skipped by the filter") fails unless `Changes` is `success` and, for each part, what `Changes` asked and what the part did are `true/success` or `false/skipped` (a part skipped though asked, one that ran though not asked, a failure, a cancel and an empty output, which is a failed `Changes`, all fail; it runs under `!cancelled()` so that a failed part makes `Build` red: a job that needs a failed one is otherwise skipped, and a skipped job passes a required check and Release's test), and it alone has `contents: write` and `packages: write` and the steps that publish (snapshot on main, release on a release tag, the website on a tag) with the conditions they always had; on a pull request it checks the parts and does nothing else. To see a decision before pushing: `node scripts/changes.mjs --list` prints every tracked path with its rule and its jobs, and `node scripts/changes.mjs --event pull_request --base origin/main --head HEAD` prints what the branch would run (the same code as CI). `Targets`, `Native`, `Release`, `Smoke` and `Publish` are as they were; a `workflow_dispatch` runs none of the six (`Changes` to `Build`). The per-job durations of a run are in the log of run 0176.

The binaries go to the GitHub release page (wave 021, run 0156, #149): `.github/workflows/ci-build.yaml` and the scripts of `.github/scripts` (bash 3.2, they run on macOS; tested with fakes by `test-release-scripts.sh` in the job `Targets` of every run). `Targets` (`release-plan.sh`, whose header lists the cases) builds `linux-amd64` only (the check `Native`) for a pull request, a push to `main` and a tag that is not a release, and the three targets of `release_targets` in `release-lib.sh` (`linux-amd64` on `ubuntu-24.04`, `linux-arm64` on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-arm64` on `macos-15`, Mandrel for JDK 25 on all three; `Native (<target>)`) for a tag whose head commit message begins `chore(release)` and for a `workflow_dispatch`. Then `Release` puts `archicode-<version>-<os>-<arch>` and `SHA256SUMS` on a DRAFT (`--generate-notes` from the previous release tag, a link to the manual's `[[upgrade-X-Y]]`), `Smoke (<target>)` tests each file as downloaded from the draft (`--version`, `views generate` on `domain_plateaus`, `editor serve`), and `Publish` publishes it (marked "Latest" only when no release tag is newer). `workflow_dispatch -f tag=archicode-X.Y.Z [-f draft=false]` rebuilds a tag and attaches to its draft (a published release is refused); with no `tag` it rehearses on a draft `rehearsal-<pom version>-<run id>` that is never published (`gh release delete <tag> --yes` after). A dispatch skips `Build` (no Maven artifact, image or website); its scripts come from the dispatched commit, the sources from the tag. Never rehearse with a test tag: every tag publishes the website.
